reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data available to confirm NK1 receptor engagement by fosaprepitant. The drug is a known NK1 antagonist with established pharmacology, but this trial provides no direct evidence of target engagement. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to assess whether NK1 receptor antagonism occurred or affected downstream tachykinin signaling. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint clearly failed - complete response rate was 1/11 (9.1%) in fosaprepitant arm vs 0/9 (0%) in placebo, showing minimal benefit. The effect size of 1.0 suggests marginal improvement but the endpoint was not met. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. Sample size was very small (N=13 total) limiting subgroup assessment. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Major confounder is the severely underpowered design with only 11 patients in treatment arm and 9 in placebo. The trial had enrollment issues per investigator commentary. High rate of serious adverse events in both arms (cardiac arrest 9.1% vs 33.3%) suggests the underlying IL-2 treatment created a challenging context, but SAE rates were actually higher in placebo arm.

failure_modes.evidence: Total sample size of only 13 patients (11 fosaprepitant, 9 placebo) is severely underpowered for detecting meaningful differences in complete response rates. Investigator noted enrollment issues.
